fixes.explanation: Teaching Isaac to run the household is a fine idea, but Abraham never asks for it here. The oath is about taking a wife for his son Isaac, and the verses say nothing about lessons. The servant already manages all that Abraham owns, so I think he's the one who could teach it. His assignment today is a lot bigger than a lesson, friend.

Relatives is it. Abraham says the servant will go to "…my country and my kindred…" and kindred means family. So Isaac's wife is to come from Abraham's own people. That's a long search for one wife, friend, and you can't just post it in a group chat.

A gate is a good guess, but it's not in this verse. The servant has the camels kneel down near the well outside the town. That's where the women go to draw water at this time of evening. So the answer is the well, friend.

Not quite, friend. The servant doesn't wait. After Rebekah fills her jar and comes up again, he runs to meet her and says, "Please let me have a little water from your jar." He's been traveling with ten camels, and I think a man like that is NOT about to stand around politely. He's RUNNING.

She doesn't stop after one jar, friend. Rebekah quickly empties her jar into the trough and runs back to the well to draw water. She keeps going until she has drawn water for all his camels. One jar. Ten camels. I get tired just carrying my mustache around the bakery, and she's out there hauling water on repeat.
